one_liner: Senior executive (SNIS) deputy running budget, contracts, HR, data governance and compliance for the National Counterterrorism Center in McLean.
fit_summary: This is a senior-executive role requiring demonstrated mastery of five ECQs plus the IC senior officer qualification, enterprise-scale resource management, and expert knowledge of IC missions and NCTC data-sharing agreements. Daniel's emergency-management consulting background and strong policy and relationship skills are relevant in spirit, but nothing on file shows executive leadership, budget authority, or intelligence community experience at this level. Daniel should apply only if the IEM role involved substantial staff, budget, and federal program leadership.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens 18+); no federal status required, but you must show all five ECQs and the ICSOCQ in a resume of no more than two pages, or be disqualified.
Bachelor's degree required (do not submit transcripts).
Must obtain a TS/SCI clearance, pass a polygraph, medical and psychological exams, and a comprehensive background investigation.

At least three years in HR, IT management, data strategy, compliance, policy development, strategic planning, mission management, federal program implementation, or CT mission work; COTR certification or enterprise contract management is also listed.
Four free-response essays of up to 200 words each, which must be written in your own words without a consultant or AI.
keywords: budget, resource, contract planning, and execution
strategy: Before investing time, honestly check whether your IEM work included supervising staff, managing budgets or contracts, and leading federal programs; without those, this SL-level role is unlikely to be reachable.
If you apply, organize the two-page resume so each ECQ and the ICSOCQ is clearly evidenced, ideally with short labeled examples, plus dates and hours per week for each job.

Frame IEM work as federal program implementation and cross-agency coordination for government clients, such as FEMA or state partners if accurate, and emphasize any contract, budget, or compliance responsibilities.
Use your policy knowledge for ECQ 1 and the Constitution essay, citing a concrete example. Write all four essays yourself, since the posting requires an AI-free certification.
Apply well before the November 12, 2026 close, attach only the listed required documents, and use this posting to identify ODNI/IC or FEMA GS-11 to GS-13 roles that fit better now.
resume_bullets: Coordinated [type of disaster recovery/preparedness program] for [government client] across [number] agencies and stakeholders, delivering [deliverable] on [timeline/budget].
Managed [scope: $ amount/number of staff/contract] including planning, tracking and reporting, resulting in [verifiable outcome].
Drafted [briefings/reports/policy analyses] for [senior audience], translating complex requirements into recommendations adopted by [client/leadership].
interview_questions: Describe a time you led a team through ambiguous requirements with multiple dependencies and high risk. What was the outcome?
How have you managed budgets or resource reductions, and how did you justify them to leadership or oversight bodies?
How would you build relationships with ODNI, DoD, and congressional stakeholders to advance NCTC priorities?
Tell us about implementing a leadership decision that differed from your own recommendation.
watch_outs: This is an executive-level position. Lacking documented senior leadership, budget, and IC experience makes selection very unlikely.
A TS/SCI clearance with polygraph is required, and the process can take many months.
The role is fully on-site in McLean with no telework, and a two-page resume limit is strictly enforced with disqualification for violations.
Short application window: October 28 to November 12, 2026.
